title: Choose an investigation approach that preserves purpose and evidence: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: What is the investigation purpose, who has authority, and how must evidence be preserved?
focalInsight: Purpose changes authority, collection, notice, preservation, disclosure, and evidence handling.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Administrative Investigation
nodes.decision: Confirm employer authority, purpose, notice, confidentiality.
nodes.failureExample: Internal issue is over-collected as criminal case.

nodes.label: Criminal Investigation
nodes.decision: Escalate via counsel/law enforcement and preserve originals.
nodes.failureExample: Responder alters disk while troubleshooting crime.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Criminal matters need early authority discipline.

nodes.label: Civil Investigation
nodes.decision: Set hold, custodians, counsel direction, discoverability.

nodes.label: Regulatory Investigation
nodes.definition: Inquiry into statutory/program duties by regulator.
nodes.detail: Inquiry into statutory/program duties by regulator.
nodes.decision: Identify remit, deadline, scope, response authority.

nodes.label: Standards Investigation
nodes.decision: Match evidence to program scope and criteria.
nodes.failureExample: Certification is treated as all legal compliance.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Standard and law have different scope.

nodes.label: Evidence Handling
nodes.decision: Record artifact, collector, time, place, method.

nodes.label: Chain Of Custody
nodes.decision: Document each transfer, custodian, time, condition.
nodes.failureExample: Drive changes hands with no record.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: It answers who held evidence when.

nodes.label: Legal Hold
nodes.definition: Direction to preserve defined relevant information.
nodes.detail: Direction to preserve defined relevant information.
nodes.decision: Identify custodians, sources, notice, release authority.

nodes.label: Investigation Scope
nodes.definition: Bounded subject, systems, time, questions, collection.
nodes.detail: Bounded subject, systems, time, questions, collection.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Scope limits intrusion and keeps relevance.

textFallback:
administrative investigation: Internal policy or employment inquiry. Decide: Confirm employer authority, purpose, notice, confidentiality. Example/failure: Internal issue is over-collected as criminal case. Retrieve: Purpose sets authorized internal process.
criminal investigation: Inquiry into suspected statutory offense. Decide: Escalate via counsel/law enforcement and preserve originals. Example/failure: Responder alters disk while troubleshooting crime. Retrieve: Criminal matters need early authority discipline.
civil investigation: Inquiry supporting claim or dispute. Decide: Set hold, custodians, counsel direction, discoverability. Example/failure: Routine deletion removes dispute records. Retrieve: Civil matters need preservation.
regulatory investigation: Inquiry into statutory/program duties by regulator. Decide: Identify remit, deadline, scope, response authority. Example/failure: Unverified estimates go to regulator. Retrieve: Use scoped accurate evidence.
standards investigation: Conformance inquiry for standard/program. Decide: Match evidence to program scope and criteria. Example/failure: Certification is treated as all legal compliance. Retrieve: Standard and law have different scope.
evidence handling: Controlled collection, preservation, access, documentation. Decide: Record artifact, collector, time, place, method. Example/failure: Log copies lose origin information. Retrieve: Explain integrity and provenance.
chain of custody: Record of possession and handling. Decide: Document each transfer, custodian, time, condition. Example/failure: Drive changes hands with no record. Retrieve: It answers who held evidence when.
legal hold: Direction to preserve defined relevant information. Decide: Identify custodians, sources, notice, release authority. Example/failure: Auto-deletion removes held chat. Retrieve: Hold suspends ordinary disposal.
investigation scope: Bounded subject, systems, time, questions, collection. Decide: Set limits before searching/interviewing. Example/failure: Unrelated personal records are searched. Retrieve: Scope limits intrusion and keeps relevance.
